GeneSummary.bullet_point: KKT24 (Tb927.10.4200) was identified as a kinetochore protein candidate that co-purified with YFP-KKT22 in immunoprecipitation experiments.
supporting_quotes: In our purification of YFP-KKT22, there was another kinetochore protein candidate (ORF Tb927.10.4200; figure 1d).

GeneSummary.bullet_point: KKT24 localizes at kinetochores from S phase to anaphase, with YFP-KKT24 signals appearing as pairs of dots in metaphase.
supporting_quotes: We found that this protein, in fact, localized at kinetochores from S phase to anaphase (figure 2a)
Note that YFP-KKT24 signals appear as pairs of dots (indicated by asterisk).

GeneSummary.bullet_point: KKT24 co-purifies with multiple KKT proteins, KKIP5, and another kinetochore protein candidate KKT25, confirming its role as a kinetochore component.
supporting_quotes: its immunoprecipitation confirmed specific co-purification with other kinetochore proteins (figure 2b)
KKT24 co-purifies with a number of KKT proteins, KKIP5, and another kinetochore protein candidate, KKT25.

GeneSummary.bullet_point: KKT24 is predicted to consist mostly of coiled coils and shares structural similarities with KKIP1, with both proteins having N-termini located at the outer region of kinetochores.
GeneSummary.evidence_location: Results section - paragraph 3 and Supplementary figure S3
supporting_quotes: Both proteins are predicted to consist mostly of coiled coils (electronic supplementary material, figure S3)
their N-termini are located at the outer region of kinetochores, as judged by the formation of pairs of dots in metaphase

GeneSummary.bullet_point: KKT24 is conserved among many kinetoplastids but is not found in free-living B. saltans or other eukaryotes.
supporting_quotes: We also note that obvious orthologues for KKT24 and KKIP1 are not found in free-living B. saltans, an organism that has essentially all of KKT1–20 proteins (table 1).

AdditionalInferences: KKT24 may function at the outer kinetochore region based on its localization pattern showing pairs of dots in metaphase, similar to KKIP1.
Despite structural similarities with KKIP1, KKT24 and KKIP1 likely do not form a stable complex based on immunoprecipitation data.
The absence of KKT24 orthologs in free-living kinetoplastids suggests it may have evolved specifically for parasitic lifestyle requirements.
KKT24's identification through KKT22 co-purification suggests these proteins may be functionally related or part of the same kinetochore subcomplex.
data.ShortSummary: KKT24 (Tb927.10.4200) is a newly identified kinetochore protein in Trypanosoma brucei that localizes to the outer kinetochore region from S phase to anaphase and co-purifies with multiple KKT proteins, representing a coiled-coil containing component conserved among parasitic kinetoplastids.
